text:
It is not Cuba, where the sea dissolves the soul.

It is not Cuba —which Gauguin never saw,

Which Picasso never saw—,

Where Black people dressed in yellow and cherry red

Roam the seawall, between two lights,

And defeated eyes

No longer disguise their thoughts.


It is not Cuba — the one that heard Stravinsky

Arrange sounds of marimbas and güiros

At the burial of Papá Montero,

Ñañigo with cane and rumbero scoundrel.


It is not Cuba — where the colonial Yankee

Cures himself of the sultriness sipping "granizados"

Of breeze, on the terraces of the development;

Where the police disinfect

The sting of the last mosquitoes

That still buzz in Spanish.


It is not Cuba — where the sea becomes transparent

So the wreckage of the Maine will not be lost,

And a revolutionary contractor

Tints the afternoon air white,

Fanning, with veteran smile,

From his rocking chair, the fragrance

Of custom-house coconuts and mangoes.

translation.title: Havana
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the satirical catalogue of Cuba, Havana, empire, music, and memory.
